seoDescription: Learn to style ASP.NET Core Razor Pages and transform a basic data display into a visually appealing website. This guide demonstrates how to use Bootstrap classes like `card-columns` and `card-body` to create a professional product layout. You'll see how to dynamically set background images using inline styles and Razor syntax, debug missing elements with browser developer tools, and apply custom CSS for a polished look.

chapters.title: Introduction: Improving the UI
chapters.description: The current product page is functional but visually unimpressive, showing a simple list of product titles; the goal is to improve the styling.

chapters.title: Applying Bootstrap Card Layout
chapters.description: The product list is wrapped in Bootstrap classes, `card-columns` and `card`, to begin structuring the content into a responsive grid of cards.

chapters.title: Dynamically Adding Product Images
chapters.description: A `div` with the `card-image` class is added, using an inline style and Razor syntax to dynamically set the background image from the product model.

chapters.title: Styling the Card Body and Title
chapters.description: The product title is moved inside a new `card-body` div and styled with an `h5` tag and a `card-title` class before running the app to check progress.

chapters.title: Debugging CSS with Browser Developer Tools
chapters.description: After running the app, the product images are missing, so the browser's 'Inspect' tool is used to diagnose the CSS and discover the images have zero height.

chapters.title: Applying Custom CSS Styles
chapters.description: A pre-written block of CSS is copied from a gist and pasted into the project's 'site.css' file to fix the image height and apply other custom styles.

chapters.title: Understanding the Shared Layout Page
chapters.description: To fix a site-wide font issue, the video introduces the '_Layout.cshtml' file, which acts as a master template for all pages, controlling shared elements like the navbar.

chapters.title: Importing Fonts and Styling the Navbar
chapters.description: A link to Google Fonts is added to the layout file's head, and the navbar's CSS classes are updated to refine its appearance and apply the new font.

chapters.title: Conclusion and Next Steps
chapters.description: The video concludes by reviewing how Razor Pages enable a seamless blend of HTML and C#, resulting in a well-styled page, and teases future enhancements.

summary:
## Styling with Bootstrap Cards

To quickly create a professional layout, wrap your data loop in **Bootstrap** classes. This structures content into a responsive card-based grid without writing complex CSS from scratch.

- **`div class="card-columns"`**: The main container that arranges cards into columns.
- **`div class="card"`**: An individual card for each product in the loop.
- **`div class="card-image"`**: A container for the product's image.
- **`div class="card-body"`**: A container for the product's text content, like the title.
- **`h5 class="card-title"`**: A styled heading for the product title.

## Using Razor Syntax for Dynamic Content

**Razor Pages** allow you to seamlessly embed C# code directly within your HTML markup. The `@` symbol is the key to switch from HTML to C#.

> [!NOTE]
> You can use Razor syntax to dynamically set HTML attributes. Here, it sets the background image URL from the product model:
> `style="background-image: url('@product.Image')"`

## Debugging CSS with Browser Tools

If visual elements don't appear as expected, your browser's developer tools are essential for debugging.

> [!TIP]
> Right-click an element and choose **"Inspect"** to view its HTML and applied CSS. In this video, inspection revealed that the product images were present but had a `height` of 0 pixels, making them invisible. You can live-edit CSS in the developer tools to quickly test fixes.

## Customizing Styles in a CSS File

While inline styles are useful for quick, dynamic styling, it's best practice to consolidate shared styles into an external stylesheet. In an ASP.NET Core project, this is typically the `site.css` file located in the `wwwroot/css` directory.

- By adding rules for classes like `.card-image` to `site.css`, you can define properties like **`height`** to ensure your layout renders correctly.
- This approach keeps your `.cshtml` files cleaner and makes styles easier to manage and reuse.

## The Shared `_Layout.cshtml` Page

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `_Layout.cshtml` file, located in the `Pages/Shared` folder, serves as the master template for your website. Changes made here will affect all pages that use it.

- It defines the overall page structure, including the `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>` tags.
- This is the ideal place to put recurring elements like the **site navigation bar (navbar)**, footer, and to link site-wide assets.
- You can add links to external resources like **Google Fonts** in the `<head>` section.
- The `@RenderBody()` method is a placeholder where the content of an individual page (like `Index.cshtml`) is injected.
